main_issue: The guideline is a sound generic template/EL-injection review pattern, but the supplied anchors and trace notes do not establish its source-to-evaluator mechanism for most assigned cases. Several anchors are validation/configuration classes with no visible template or expression sink, and the evidence explicitly says it is not exploit proof.
split_suggestions: Verified untrusted template or expression text reaching a template/EL evaluator, with sandbox, reflection, method-invocation, or template-selection controls missing
Validation, notifier, or configuration cases whose actual vulnerability mechanism must be established from patch and dataflow evidence before assignment
evidence_notes: JinjavaBeanELResolver is plausibly aligned with restricted EL/property-resolution controls, but the payload provides no untrusted-input source or evaluator call.

Ballcat generator and Velocity/Freemarker rendering anchors are plausibly template-related, but they do not show whether attackers can control template text, template selection, or only ordinary rendering data.
BrowserUp LongPositiveConstraint and the Dropwizard SelfValidating/ViolationCollector anchors appear validation-focused; no template engine or expression-evaluation sink is shown.
Spring Boot Admin DingTalkNotifier and Hibernate BaseHibernateValidatorConfiguration could involve expression/configuration handling, but the supplied windows do not demonstrate that mechanism.
All case trace notes verify patch-derived review-entry anchors only; they cannot substantiate a shared source, sink, missing guard, exploit precondition, or safe fix.
